Repo: /Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier (Next.js app — note it's a newer Next.js version; docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/). Feature to plan: on the /sites list page, add a column with a "Download" action per row that zips the site's files (stored in S3 under a folder named by the slug) and streams the zip to the browser.

Please report, with file paths and key line numbers/snippets:
1. The /sites page: its file(s), how the list/table is rendered (component, columns, data source), and how rows are typed.
2. The S3 access layer: client setup, functions for listing objects under a slug prefix, getting objects, uploading (the upload path probably unzips archives — note which zip library is used and how).
3. Existing route handlers / API routes (app/api/...), and how auth (Cloudflare Access) is enforced on them (middleware/proxy, helpers).
4. Testing conventions: Jest setup, how S3 is mocked (aws-sdk-client-mock? manual mocks?), example tests for route handlers and for UI components (Testing Library?).
5. package.json dependencies relevant to zipping (archiver, jszip, fflate, yauzl, adm-zip, etc.) and AWS SDK.
6. Any slug validation helper.
Medium thoroughness. Read-only.

# Atelier

## Overview

Atelier is a service internal to Artsy and Artnet, intended for dead-simple hosting of static html sites, such as might be produced by non-technical users with the assistance of LLMs and coding agents. Or indeed any static html, hand-coded, vibe-coded, generated, etc.

The inspirations are:

- [Quick](https://shopify.engineering/quick) — Shopify's version, for internal use
- [Drop](https://www.cloudflare.com/drop/) — Cloudflare's version, for public use

## Project Goals

- **Dead-simple UX**: drag a zip archive containing html/css/js onto a webpage, see it live in a few seconds

- **Simple naming conventions**: user supplies a slug e.g. `marketing-dashboard` which becomes the name of the folder where the assets are stored as well as the subdomain of the public url from which the site can be accessed, e.g. `marketing-dashboard.atelier.artsy.dev`

- **Comically simple permissions**: access is to the entire system, uploads and websites, is gated to only verified Artsy users. But once in, anyone can freely write and overwrite any folder, any project after confirmation they _intend_ to overwrite an existing upload.

Simple, simple, simple!

### Code quality

- All code is well-typed
- All code tested via Jest, and introduced via TDD
- All code linted via Biome, automatically on file-save and enforced at commit time
- CircleCI (`.circleci/config.yml`) runs `yarn test` on every push, and deploys via Hokusai: `main` to staging, `release` to production (behind a Horizon release block). It does not run lint or typecheck — run those locally before pushing.
- Additionally: an on-demand `@claude`-mention workflow (`.github/workflows/claude-review.yml`) runs a Claude Code review when someone comments `@claude` on a PR. It doesn't run on every push and isn't a substitute for the CircleCI pipeline.

### Commit hygiene

- All commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- Commits are as small and cohesive as reasonably possible. Prefer <500 LOC
- All agent-authored commits include a trailer e.g.
  - `Assisted-by: Claude:Sonnet-5`
  - `Assisted-by: Claude:Opus-4.8`

### Branch and PR hygiene

- All PR titles follow Conventional Commits
- This repo enforces **linear history, rebase-merge only** on `main`. Before starting new work (and before committing anything already in progress), check whether the current branch is the right base:
  1. `git branch --show-current` — if it's not `main` and isn't a branch created for the task at hand, stop and check further before committing.
  2. `git log --oneline main..<branch>` — if this shows commits, the branch has work not yet on `main`. Check whether that work is an **open PR** (`gh pr list --head <branch>` or ask the developer) rather than assuming it's abandoned or already merged.
  3. Once `main` reflects the intended base, create a fresh branch off it for the new work: `git checkout -b <new-branch>`. Untracked files in the working tree survive a branch switch, so any not-yet-committed new files carry over safely — but confirm with `git status` before and after.
  4. Never `git rebase`, force-push, or otherwise rewrite shared history without explicit developer instruction, given the rebase-merge-only policy.
  5. Do not self-merge PRs. PRs require review from a human and/or a separate agent. Do not @-mention Claude to trigger reviews, that is for a human to do.

### Github hygiene

- When opening a PR or Issue on developer's behalf, also use the `Assisted-by:` trailer in the PR description
- When posting a comment on developer's behalf, use a similar `Posted-by:` header at the top of the comment
- When starting a task on the Github Project, always change its Status to In Progress. If you learn that a PR is merged, confirm the task's status is Done.

### Project board

Work is tracked as GitHub Issues on the [project board](https://github.com/orgs/artsy/projects/10) project, not in local docs.

- Use `gh project` to interact with projects
- Use the `chore` label for non-code tasks, and assign them to your developer
- Use `epic` field to group related tasks. Epics follow a `00 Name` zero-padded naming convention

### Other notes

- Note that you cannot run `aws` commands yourself due to role-based access and OTPs. Always ask the developer to run `aws` commands for you.

## Further reading

- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — infrastructure and design
  decisions (Cloudflare Access, CloudFront + S3, caching, risks)
- Task tracking lives in the
  [Atelier GitHub project](https://github.com/orgs/artsy/projects/10),

- **Simple naming conventions**: user supplies a slug e.g. `marketing-dashboard` which becomes the name of the folder where the assets are stored as well as the subdomain of the public url from which the site can be accessed, e.g. `marketing-dashboard.atelier.artsy.dev`

- **Comically simple permissions**: access is to the entire system, uploads and websites, is gated to only verified Artsy users. But once in, anyone can freely write and overwrite any folder, any project after confirmation they _intend_ to overwrite an existing upload.

Simple, simple, simple!

### Code quality

- All code is well-typed
- All code tested via Jest, and introduced via TDD
- All code linted via Biome, automatically on file-save and enforced at commit time
- CircleCI (`.circleci/config.yml`) runs `yarn test` on every push, and deploys via Hokusai: `main` to staging, `release` to production (behind a Horizon release block). It does not run lint or typecheck — run those locally before pushing.
- Additionally: an on-demand `@claude`-mention workflow (`.github/workflows/claude-review.yml`) runs a Claude Code review when someone comments `@claude` on a PR. It doesn't run on every push and isn't a substitute for the CircleCI pipeline.

### Commit hygiene

- All commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- Commits are as small and cohesive as reasonably possible. Prefer <500 LOC
- All agent-authored commits include a trailer e.g.
  - `Assisted-by: Claude:Sonnet-5`
  - `Assisted-by: Claude:Opus-4.8`

### Branch and PR hygiene

- All PR titles follow Conventional Commits
- This repo enforces **linear history, rebase-merge only** on `main`. Before starting new work (and before committing anything already in progress), check whether the current branch is the right base:
  1. `git branch --show-current` — if it's not `main` and isn't a branch created for the task at hand, stop and check further before committing.
  2. `git log --oneline main..<branch>` — if this shows commits, the branch has work not yet on `main`. Check whether that work is an **open PR** (`gh pr list --head <branch>` or ask the developer) rather than assuming it's abandoned or already merged.
  3. Once `main` reflects the intended base, create a fresh branch off it for the new work: `git checkout -b <new-branch>`. Untracked files in the working tree survive a branch switch, so any not-yet-committed new files carry over safely — but confirm with `git status` before and after.
  4. Never `git rebase`, force-push, or otherwise rewrite shared history without explicit developer instruction, given the rebase-merge-only policy.
  5. Do not self-merge PRs. PRs require review from a human and/or a separate agent. Do not @-mention Claude to trigger reviews, that is for a human to do.

### Github hygiene

- When opening a PR or Issue on developer's behalf, also use the `Assisted-by:` trailer in the PR description
- When posting a comment on developer's behalf, use a similar `Posted-by:` header at the top of the comment
- When starting a task on the Github Project, always change its Status to In Progress. If you learn that a PR is merged, confirm the task's status is Done.

### Project board

Work is tracked as GitHub Issues on the [project board](https://github.com/orgs/artsy/projects/10) project, not in local docs.

- Use `gh project` to interact with projects
- Use the `chore` label for non-code tasks, and assign them to your developer
- Use `epic` field to group related tasks. Epics follow a `00 Name` zero-padded naming convention

### Other notes

- Note that you cannot run `aws` commands yourself due to role-based access and OTPs. Always ask the developer to run `aws` commands for you.

## Further reading

- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — infrastructure and design
  decisions (Cloudflare Access, CloudFront + S3, caching, risks)
- Task tracking lives in the
  [Atelier GitHub project](https://github.com/orgs/artsy/projects/10),
  not in these docs

The app uses the **Pages Router**, not the App Router. Pages and API routes are `src/pages/**/*.page.ts(x)`, set by `pageExtensions` in `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/next.config.js:12`. There is no `app/` directory and no `middleware.ts` or `proxy.ts`. A download endpoint would therefore be a Pages API route, e.g. `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/pages/api/sites/[slug]/download.page.ts` (my suggestion; it doesn't exist yet). It would stream the zip through `res`.

## 1. The /sites page
- **Page:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/pages/sites.page.tsx`
  - `getServerSideProps` (lines 124-136) calls `listSites(getS3Client(), s3Bucket, sort)` and maps each result through `toSiteListing`.
  - Props are `{ sites: SiteListing[]; sort: SiteSort; view: "list" | "grid" }` (lines 33-37).
  - The view defaults to grid; `?view=list` switches to the table (`parseView`, line 50).
  - Grid view renders `<SiteCard>` in a `<ul>` (lines 188-204). List view renders `<SiteTable sites={sites} />` (line 206). If the download should also appear in grid view, `SiteCard.tsx` needs it too.
- **Table:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/components/SiteTable.tsx`
  - It's a styled `<table>`. The `<thead>` is visually hidden but still read by screen readers (lines 22-29).
  - Headings are hard-coded at line 56: `["Preview", "Slug", "Uploaded by", "Uploaded"]`.
  - Each row has four `Cell`s: thumbnail, slug link via `SiteLink`, uploader, and a right-aligned relative time (lines 68-107).
  - `Cell` has `&:last-child { padding-right: 0 }` (lines 31-40), so a new last column takes over that rule.
- **Row types:**
  - `SiteInfo { slug; uploadedBy?; uploadedAt? }` in `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/sites.ts:5-9`.
  - `SiteListing extends SiteInfo { url; thumbnailUrl }` in `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/siteListing.ts:4-7`.
  - `toSiteListing` (siteListing.ts:27) builds the URLs. Thumbnail URLs are `/api/thumbnails/${slug}?v=<uploadedAt>`. A `downloadUrl` field could be added the same way, or built inline in the component.

## 2. S3 access layer
- **Client setup:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/deps.ts`
  - Module-level singletons: `getConfig()` and `getS3Client()` (a `new S3Client({ region })`), plus `getCloudFrontClient()`.
  - `resetDeps()` exists for tests.
- **`/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/s3.ts`.** Every function takes `(client, bucket, slug, ...)`.
  - `listPrefix(client, bucket, slug): Promise<string[]>` (lines 59-84): paginated `ListObjectsV2` with `Prefix: \`${slug}/\``. It returns full keys including the `slug/` prefix.
  - `headIndex` (35-57) reads `uploaded-by` and `uploaded-at` metadata from `${slug}/index.html`.
  - `listSlugs` (86-110) lists with delimiter `/` and drops anything `validateSlug` rejects.
  - `deletePrefix` (112-142).
  - `putFile` (144-168) writes key `${slug}/${path}` with metadata.
  - `putThumbnail` and `getThumbnail` (170-202) use `_thumbnails/${slug}.jpg`. That's outside the slug prefix (lines 29-33), so `listPrefix` won't include thumbnails in a download.
- **There is no general get-object function.** `getThumbnail` is the only `GetObjectCommand` user, and it buffers with `Body.transformToByteArray()`. For streaming, a new helper such as `getObjectStream(client, bucket, key)` would return `Body` as a Node `Readable`. `isNotFound` (lines 19-27) can be reused.
- **Upload and unzip:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/zip.ts`
  - Uses **`unzipper`** (`unzipper.Parse()` on a stream, line 35).
  - `extractZip(source, maxTotalBytes)` buffers every entry into `{ path, content: Buffer }[]`, rejects zip-slip paths (`normalizeEntryPath`, lines 12-29), and enforces a byte limit.
  - `normalizeZipEntries` strips macOS junk, removes a common root folder, and copies a sole root `.html` file to `index.html`.
- **Upload flow:**
  - Busboy streams the multipart request into `extractZip` (`/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/parseUpload.ts`).
  - `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/pages/api/upload.page.ts` then validates, deletes the prefix, calls `putFile` per entry, and invalidates CloudFront.
  - When `index.html` is an alias, it's stored as an extra copy with `aliased-from` metadata (lines 155-164). A download will therefore include both `index.html` and the original file.

## 3. API routes and auth
- **Routes:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/pages/api/`
  - `check.page.ts`, `sites.page.ts`, `status.page.ts`, `upload.page.ts`, `thumbnails/[slug].page.ts`.
  - All use `(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse)` wrapped in `withErrorHandler`.
- **Template to copy:** `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/pages/api/thumbnails/[slug].page.ts`
  - Returns 405 for any method other than GET.
  - Reads the slug with `typeof req.query.slug === "string" ? ... : ""`, then calls `validateSlug` and returns 400 if it fails.
  - Calls `getS3Client()` and `getConfig().s3Bucket`, sets headers, and sends the response.
- **`withErrorHandler`** (`/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/middleware/withErrorHandler.ts`) returns a JSON 500. If headers were already sent it just calls `res.end()` (lines 10-12). That matters for streaming: an error mid-stream leaves a truncated zip, not an error response.
- **Auth is not enforced in app code.** Cloudflare Access protects all of `*.artsy.dev` at the edge (`/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:43-51`). The app only reads the `Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email` header, falling back to `X-Requested-By`, and uses it for attribution, never for access control. This uses `getHeader` in `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/getHeader.ts`, called at upload.page.ts:127-138. A download route under `/api/` gets the same edge protection with no extra code. If you want logging, copy upload's pattern: `console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: ... }))`.

- `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `@aws-sdk/client-cloudfront` ^3.1088.0.

## 6. Slug validation
- `/Users/roop/src/artsy/atelier/src/lib/slug.ts` exports `validateSlug(slug): { valid; error? }`.
  - Pattern `/^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$/` plus a reserved-name list.
  - It runs in both server and browser.
- **Gotcha:** `gallery` is a reserved slug (slug.ts:20), yet the `SiteTable` and sites page test fixtures use `gallery`. That's harmless for UI tests, but a download-route test with `gallery` would get a 400.
